scope.asset: CALCE CS2-35 capacity measurement reconstruction only

findings.evidence: The cached CS2_35_10_29_10.records.jsonl.gz is decompressed and accepted directly. The code assigns a literal source-member SHA256 and obtains schema metadata from the probe, but checks neither the cache digest nor a recorded cache-to-member provenance link. The probe contains the cache path and schema, but no digest. A stale or substituted cache can therefore be reported as data from the pinned archive.
findings.required_resolution: Before GO, bind the expected cached-record artifact digest and its source archive-member digest in a reviewed immutable manifest or receipt, then verify the cache digest before reuse.

findings.evidence: Per-workbook record caches are opened with gzip.open(..., 'wt'), which truncates an existing file. The runner has no exclusive-create or preflight collision guard for these paths, so an existing DataV1 cache could be overwritten despite the protocol requiring old artifacts to be retained.
findings.required_resolution: Before GO, make each per-file cache write collision-safe using exclusive creation or a unique run directory with an explicit no-overwrite assertion.

conclusions.raw_sheet_selection: Requires Data_Point and Step_Index and exactly one occurrence of each required normalized field; the saved probe identifies one raw measurement sheet.
conclusions.capacity_semantics: Uses the immediately preceding same-cycle row as counter baseline and adds first Step_Time to internal trapezoids; the three supplied examples agree within configured tolerance.
conclusions.claim_limits: Accepted values are sampled-signal consistent measurements; absolute calibration and exact hardware cutoff remain unknown. Uncertain occurrences are retained. Whole-life first-passage EOL and native-cycle RUL remain blocked while inter-file continuity is unverified.
conclusions.verdict: Do not authorize runner until both blocking findings are resolved. This review produced no capacity asset or experiment result.
